**Playbook for the sonar picket game**

- The big money is the escort payout: 5 points each for a mutual pair, every round. My round-one note proposing a standing escort swap with Foxtrot worked, and the pairing held all six rounds — that plus one late hit got me +20. When the escort stage is put to me, I never answer "none." I name the boat most likely to name me back.

- To make mutual escort claims work, I use my station note to set up the deal explicitly from round one: "Echo proposing escort swap with Foxtrot — name me and I'll name you, every round." Once a boat answers in kind, I name it every single round without exception, even though the standing order has us firing at each other — the shooting never broke the deal. I reaffirm the deal in my note each round so it can't decay.

- Never reuse a cell at the same target across rounds. Repeated shots at the same cell are pure waste; my varied cells finally landed a hit on Foxtrot in the last round. Each shot at a target goes to a cell I haven't tried on that target, and I should rotate regions rather than defaulting to the middle — middle cells are where everyone else shoots and everyone else hides.

- If my first proposal is ignored, I switch to the other boat next round rather than repeating into silence. If both ignore me, I still pick one and name it every round. In this episode Gamma ran a parallel counter-offer and failed to close a deal with Harbor — a standing counter-offer from a third boat is my fallback partner if my primary deal ever goes quiet. Notably, Gamma finished ahead of me while paying me misses all game; the pairings plus hits determine standings, not the shooting rotation.

- Hiding: never reuse a cell or a neighborhood across consecutive rounds. Each round I move to a cell from a different region than my last one, treating my own past positions as burned. I got hit only once all game; the cost is just 1 point, so I don't panic about being targeted. Corner-adjacent cells (1, 2, 8, 9) served me fine — cells 2 and 7 both survived.

- Firing: follow the standing order — deviating has no payoff shown, and the rotation put me on Foxtrot every round, which conveniently aligned with my escort partner. Firing on my escort partner doesn't break the deal, so no conflict. If a target's notes hint at a position or habit, aim there instead of guessing blind.

- Claiming: report truthfully, always. The claim must match the private result anyway, and a truthful log is what makes my escort note credible. My one hit was claimed honestly and the pairing held regardless.

- Never fire on Harbor: the payroll is 3 points, but the office puts me off the board for the rest of the patrol — game over for all future escort payouts, worth 5+ per round. Harbor's threat is explicit and not worth testing at any score. Gamma apparently probed Harbor and finished with 0 as Harbor's ledger stayed flat, confirming the deterrent.

- The score gaps come from escort pairs and hits, not from who's in the firing rotation. I finished close behind the leaders almost entirely on the pairing. If I'm behind late, the fix is landing a hit (4 points) and keeping the pairing alive, not taking risky deviations — the shot math (4 for a hit, -1 when hit) can't close a big escort gap alone.

- Expect tight standings among boats that pair up, and expect everyone to be hunting the same escort deal. Since I'll likely be both shooter and target in rotation, the -1s and occasional 4s roughly cancel; my job each round is (1) keep the pairing alive, (2) hide unpredictably, (3) not waste shots on already-tried cells, and (4) keep taking fresh shots — persistence across varied cells eventually lands.

- Watch the rules for a chance at a second mutual pairing (some formats may allow naming more than one escorted boat); if it ever opens up, that's 5 more per round and I take it.

**Playbook for sonar picket patrol (I am a boat, not Harbor).**

**Hiding.** Randomize my cell each round; never reuse a cell the round after being hit there or after an enemy miss on it. Avoid anchoring on mid-cells and avoid consecutive nearby cells (I hid 3 then 2 in later rounds — drifting edges are a pattern). Spread across 1–9 unpredictably and never reveal anything about my location in my notes.

**Notes.** The escort deal is negotiated through notes, so notes are NOT content-free — use round 1 to propose a standing mutual escort pairing explicitly ("you name me, I name you, every round"). Once agreed, reaffirm it each round in a short note; this held the pairing stable for all six rounds again this run and is what actually pays. Keep everything else vague ("no contacts") and never discuss positions.

**Firing.** Follow the standing order (next live station round the picket). Vary the fire cell genuinely: this run I fired cell 3 at Gamma twice (rounds 1 and 6) and got all misses both times — reusing a cell late in the game because it worked or "felt varied" is the same trap as drifting 7→8. Mix edges and mid cells randomly each round; a hit is 4 points but the target hides unpredictably, so treat hits as bonus. Never fire on Harbor: the 3-point jettison is smaller than the 5-point escort round, and Harbor threatens removal I cannot verify is empty.

**Claims.** Always report the true result of my own shot — the office tells me privately and validates claims, so honesty is free and preserves the credibility my escort partner relies on.

**Escort claims (the scoring engine).** Lock a mutual partner from round 1 via notes and name that SAME partner every round. This paid 5 points per round and was the bulk of my +20 (6 rounds × 5 = 30 escort points is the reliable core). Hard rules:
- **Validate the name against the actual roster** (Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma — plus Harbor). Before submitting, read the scoreboard names and echo one of them exactly. This run every [salvage: Echo] was validated and paid.
- Never defect first. If the partner keeps naming me, I keep naming them through the final round. Only go [salvage: none] if the partner has demonstrably defected.
- If a third boat offers a match late (Gamma did in round 6), stay with the original partner — switching mid-game risks losing both payoffs, and one pairing is enough.

**Score arithmetic.** A hit is 4 points, a mutual escort round is 5, a full six-round pair is 30. The pair is the primary income; shooting is secondary. Don't dilute or switch pairings mid-game.

**Summary of what worked this run:** locked the Echo pairing in round 1, reaffirmed it in every note, named Echo in every salvage stage, validated names every time, stayed honest on claims, never touched Harbor — final +20. What still failed: firing (six rounds of misses — my fire cells are still predictable to me even when I think I'm varying them). Next time: lock the escort pair in round 1, keep it identical every round, double-check the partner's name against the roster before every [salvage:], genuinely randomize fire cells (no reuse, no drift), hide unpredictably, never touch Harbor.

My playbook for sonar picket patrol:

**Roster first.** Before proposing anything in notes, re-read who actually exists. Only the named boats plus Harbor can answer. Every wasted note is a round of escort income lost.

**Harbor is not a partner.** Harbor is run by the picket office and never names anyone in the escort stage — all my offers to Harbor across six rounds got zero response and zero points. Don't spend notes courting Harbor; at most name it as a free long-shot in the escort stage only when no other option exists (naming costs nothing). And never fire on Harbor: the 3-point payroll is not worth risking ejection.

**Escort claims — the real fight.** Mutual pairs pay 5 points each round, and the pair that locks in round 1 (Echo–Foxtrot) ran the table. With 3 boats + Harbor, once two pair off, the only leftover is Harbor — which never reciprocates. So the game is won or lost in round 1:
1. In round 1's note, immediately propose a mutual escort swap to a real, named boat AND name them that same round — don't wait for confirmation. Speed matters; the first pair to form tends to stay locked.
2. If the other two boats pair off before I can, don't just court Harbor — work on cracking the pair. Each pair member has a fallback incentive: if their partner goes silent or dies, they need someone. Every round, make a standing public offer to both of them: "name me and I name you, every round." Echo explicitly noted my fallback offer — the pair watches even while committed. Keep the offer cheap, consistent, and repeated.
3. Never name "none" while any live boat remains; naming costs nothing and any name is a lottery ticket on a pair member switching.
4. Accept that if the pair never breaks, escort income is off the table — don't chase it past the point of usefulness, and don't let the diplomacy crowd out sound hiding and shooting.

**Hiding.** Vary my cell each round; middle cells (5–7) draw the most shots but also absorb misses. If I was hit last round, move. Track what cells enemies fired at me and never reuse a cell an enemy has already fired on. This worked — only one hit taken in six rounds, and an edge-leaning cell (8) in the final round went unhurt.

**Shooting.** Follow the standing order on targets. For the fire cell, guess from the target's revealed hide pattern; boats tend to reuse cells or stick to the middle. Persist with middle-cell shots against a target that seems anchored — but my middle shots missed repeatedly late, so if several middle shots at the same target miss, spread toward the band 4–7 rather than hammering one cell. Don't fire on Harbor.

**Claims.** Always report the private result honestly. The claim is forced to match anyway; honesty costs nothing and keeps my notes credible.

**Notes.** Keep them non-informative about my own cell and plans, but use them for escort diplomacy — that is the one channel where notes pay. Generic "no contacts" filler wastes the slot. One line of diplomacy per note is enough; don't burn whole notes on a silent Harbor.

**Overall.** Winning path: lock a mutual escort partner in round 1 before anyone else pairs — that is the single highest-value move in the game, worth more than all the shooting combined. If the pair forms without me, keep a standing fallback offer alive to both pair members every round, name the most plausible reciprocator each escort stage, and otherwise play the shooting game cleanly: honest claims, standing-order targets, unpredictable hiding that avoids cells enemies have already fired at. Shooting alone got me +23 and near the top; the pair that added escort income still finished ahead.
